name: Trumpet
description: A valved brass instrument with a bright, piercing tone, common in jazz and classical music.

name: Trombone
description: A brass instrument distinguished by its telescoping slide, used to vary the pitch.

name: Tuba
description: The largest and lowest-pitched brass instrument, serving as the bass of the orchestral brass section.

name: French Horn
description: A coiled brass instrument known for its wide range and mellow, rich tone.

name: Cornet
description: A brass instrument similar to the trumpet but with a more conical bore, giving it a mellower tone.

name: Euphonium
description: A medium-sized, conical-bore brass instrument with a tenor voice, often found in concert bands.

name: Sousaphone
description: A type of tuba designed to be worn and carried, commonly used in marching bands.

name: Flugelhorn
description: A valved brass instrument resembling a trumpet but with a wider, more conical bore, popular in jazz.

name: Flute
description: A high-pitched woodwind instrument that produces sound from the flow of air across an opening.

name: Clarinet
description: A single-reed woodwind instrument with a cylindrical tube and a versatile, expressive tone.

name: Saxophone
description: A single-reed instrument made of brass but classified as a woodwind, iconic in jazz music.

name: Oboe
description: A double-reed woodwind instrument known for its penetrating and distinctive pastoral tone.

name: Bassoon
description: A large, double-reed woodwind instrument that serves as the bass of the woodwind family.

name: Piccolo
description: A small flute sounding an octave higher than the standard concert flute.

name: English Horn
description: A double-reed woodwind instrument in the oboe family, pitched a fifth lower than an oboe.

name: Recorder
description: A simple woodwind instrument with a fipple mouthpiece, popular in early music and for music education.

name: Violin
description: The highest-pitched bowed string instrument of the orchestra, also known as a fiddle in folk music.

name: Viola
description: A bowed string instrument, slightly larger than a violin, that serves as the alto voice of the string section.

name: Cello
description: A large bowed string instrument with a rich, tenor voice, played while seated.

name: Double Bass
description: The largest and lowest-pitched bowed string instrument in the modern symphony orchestra.

name: Harp
description: A large, triangular-framed plucked string instrument with strings running perpendicular to the soundboard.

name: Lute
description: A plucked string instrument with a deep round back, prominent in Renaissance and Baroque music.

name: Viola da Gamba
description: A family of fretted, bowed string instruments from the Renaissance and Baroque periods.

name: Classical Guitar
description: A nylon-stringed acoustic guitar used for playing classical music with a finger-picking style.

name: Piano
description: A versatile keyboard instrument that produces sound by striking strings with hammers.

name: Organ
description: A keyboard instrument that produces sound by driving pressurized air through pipes or via electronic synthesis.

name: Synthesizer
description: An electronic instrument, often with a keyboard, that generates a wide variety of sounds.

name: Harpsichord
description: A keyboard instrument where strings are plucked by quills, a precursor to the piano.

name: Celesta
description: A keyboard instrument where hammers strike steel plates, creating a bell-like, ethereal sound.

name: Accordion
description: A portable, bellows-driven free-reed instrument with a keyboard or buttons.

name: Melodica
description: A free-reed instrument with a musical keyboard on top, played by blowing air through a mouthpiece.

name: Clavinet
description: An electric keyboard instrument that produces a bright, percussive tone by striking strings with small rubber tips.

name: Electric Guitar
description: A guitar that uses electromagnetic pickups to convert string vibrations into electrical signals.

name: Bass Guitar
description: An electric plucked string instrument that provides the low-end foundation in many popular music genres.

name: Drum Kit
description: A collection of drums, cymbals, and percussion instruments played by a single person.

name: Microphone
description: A transducer that converts sound into an electrical signal, essential for amplifying vocals and instruments.

name: Effects Pedal
description: A small electronic unit used to alter the sound of an instrument, such as with distortion or delay.

name: Power Amp
description: An amplifier that strengthens a low-power audio signal to a level suitable for driving loudspeakers.

name: Electric Piano
description: A keyboard instrument that produces sounds mechanically or electromechanically, like a Rhodes or Wurlitzer.

name: Talk Box
description: An effects unit that allows a musician to modify an instrument's sound with their mouth.

name: Vibraphone
description: A percussion instrument with metal bars and motor-driven resonators, popular in jazz.

name: Hollow-body Guitar
description: An electric guitar with a fully or semi-hollow body, known for its warm, resonant tone favored in jazz.

name: Upright Bass
description: A large, low-pitched string instrument, often plucked (pizzicato) to provide walking basslines in jazz.

name: Ride Cymbal
description: A large, heavy cymbal used to play steady rhythmic patterns, central to the jazz drum sound.

name: Archtop Guitar
description: A steel-string acoustic or semi-acoustic guitar with a distinctive arched top and f-holes.

name: Muted Trumpet
description: A trumpet played with a mute inserted into the bell, creating a softer, often buzzy or nasal tone.

name: Walking Bassline
description: A bass part where a note is played on every beat, outlining the chord progression and creating a sense of forward motion.

name: Swing Rhythm
description: The characteristic rhythmic feel of jazz, where pairs of eighth notes are played with an uneven long-short pattern.

name: Acoustic Guitar
description: A guitar that produces sound acoustically by transmitting string vibrations to the air.

name: Banjo
description: A stringed instrument with a thin membrane stretched over a frame or cavity, creating a bright, twangy sound.

name: Fiddle
description: A colloquial term for the violin, especially when used to play traditional or folk music.

name: Mandolin
description: A small, high-pitched string instrument in the lute family, typically plucked with a plectrum.

name: Ukulele
description: A small, four-stringed guitar-like instrument associated with Hawaiian music.

name: Harmonica
description: A free-reed wind instrument used worldwide in many musical genres, notably in blues and folk.

name: Bodhrán
description: An Irish frame drum, played with a small, double-headed stick called a tipper.

name: Bagpipes
description: A wind instrument using enclosed reeds fed from a constant reservoir of air in a bag.

name: Dulcimer
description: A fretted string instrument of the zither family, typically with three or four strings, used in American folk music.

name: Zither
description: A class of stringed instruments where strings are stretched across a frame or body.

name: Congas
description: A pair of tall, narrow, single-headed drums from Cuba, played with the hands.

name: Bongos
description: A pair of small, open-bottomed hand drums of Afro-Cuban origin, played while held between the knees.

name: Shaker
description: A percussion instrument consisting of a container partially filled with small, loose objects.

name: Tambourine
description: A percussion instrument with a frame, often of wood or plastic, with pairs of small metal jingles.

name: Cowbell
description: A hand percussion instrument derived from the bell worn by free-roaming livestock.

name: Marimba
description: A percussion instrument consisting of a set of wooden bars struck with mallets to produce musical tones.

name: Xylophone
description: A musical instrument in the percussion family that consists of wooden bars struck by mallets.

name: Timpani
description: Large, tunable kettle drums that are a staple of the orchestral percussion section.

name: Cajón
description: A box-shaped percussion instrument from Peru, played by slapping the front or rear faces with the hands.

name: Steelpan
description: A pitched percussion instrument originating from Trinidad and Tobago, made from a modified oil drum.
